The thesis
$0 a year

committed to content before an audience is consulted.

Today the first real audience test is a $25K screening at rough cut, when 96% of the budget is spent. Trailer Park moves the test to the script — 1% spent — by rendering a premise into a 30-second trailer and reading how people choose.

$255B: Ampere Analysis, global content spend. Screening cost and spend curve: industry norms, illustrative.

Cold open

The last three times a trailer decided a movie.

2014DeadpoolTest footage leaked online. The reaction greenlit a film the studio had shelved.
2013Veronica Mars91,585 fans put up $5.7M before a frame was shot.
2019Sonic the HedgehogOne trailer's reaction sent the character back to the drawing board — and moved the release three months.

Each was an accident. Trailer Park makes it the method — and puts unmade scripts in a room with films you already know, so every read has a scale.

The greenlight supply chain

The audience is asked last.

Writers and crews absorb the risk; the money flows to known IP because known IP is the only thing with a number attached.

A 30-second render costs about $30. A read from four hundred people costs less than $200. The number arrives before the option is signed.

Render cost ~$0.24/s at 720p; verify current provider pricing before quoting.

The insight

Reading a premise explains <2% of what happens. Watching it is the test.

ρ = 0.135
text-only score vs realised performance, 9,901 titles — under 2% of variance. Published as our own baseline, so the audience read has to beat it.

AI video makes a premise watchable for cents. That moves the test from the end of the chain to the start — and it's back-testable on films that already exist.

Illustrative. Fictional title. Real certificates cite the published back-test and released comparables.

The choice is a choice: a Bradley-Terry rank a research head can audit. Completion, walk-away and replay ride alongside as creative notes, never inside the number.

Every read is written to a ledger that later joins to what actually happened — box office, streaming, licensing — through a certified title spine. That join is the moat: nobody else has draft-stage reads on titles that were later made.

Three sides, one certificate

Give · Get · Keep.

● Now · ◐ After the proof · ○ Later. Trailer Park never pitches, represents or negotiates, and cannot promise a script gets made.

Gate Zero · pass or fail

The bar is frozen before we run it.

text baseline ρ 0.135
PASS: text + 0.10
?

Two hundred released films, rendered from their scripts and retitled, read blind by a recruited panel with a recognition probe. Two render styles, so we learn which one predicts. Pre-registered; ~$18K; result published pass or fail.

Then a two-week, $2,500 fan test: six teasers, three hundred horror fans, one pair a night. Unprompted return ≥ 25% and test-retest ≥ 75% or the consumer side isn't built as designed.
